answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated way, evidence links their actions and triggers a penalty proportional to k² (O(k²)), rather than treating each as an isolated fault. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the cohort’s escrow, with asymmetric depreciation preventing rapid recovery. Thus, splitting control across sybils sharply increases expected loss; velvet, pearl, and opal labels do not conceal common control.
